document.title: Airplane Flight Manual Supplement
document.pitch: 150 cm (59.1 in) at station 65.6 cm (25.8 in)
document.static_rpm_note: Static rpm at full throttle, ISA, SL, no wind (carburetor heat off and mixture leaned to max. rpm): 2000 to 2200 rpm
document.approval: Performance Data is not TCCA Approved.
document.scope: No change to the basic airplane except Cruise Performance.

digitization.method: Axes calibrated from sub-pixel grid-line peaks, converted with piecewise-linear interpolation between major ticks (eliminates residual of a global linear fit). Curves traced from the original embedded JPEGs (not the upsampled 300 DPI page render). Nearly-straight curves were RANSAC-fitted (x = a + b y or y = a + b x); mildly curved Fig 3 %BHP curves and the Full Throttle envelope were walked with a slope-constrained nearest-peak tracker and fitted with a quadratic or cubic in y when the RMSE was below 1.5 px. Additional Fig 2 endpoints were read as off-grid peaks on the original image to complete printed extents near labels.

fig1_da_ft.note: 1 px ≈ 36 ft. Linear-fit RMSE ≈ 0.8–1.1 px. Printed example is a computed value (7391), not a chart reading.

fig2_rpm.note: 1 px ≈ 1.5 RPM. Fit RMSE 0.5–1.1 px. Example residual −1.3 RPM.

fig3_tas_kt.note: 1 px ≈ 0.13 kt. Quadratic/cubic RMSE 0.30–0.42 px. Example residual +0.12 kt.

uncertainty.fig4_table: Exact printed integers and one-decimal GPH; no digitization uncertainty except as noted for two physically suspicious GPH cells.

fig1_density_altitude.note: The printed 7391 ft is a computed value (1 ft precision), not a chart reading. The NWS/NOAA density-altitude formula DA = 145442.16 * (1 - ((17.326*P_inHg)/(459.67+T_F))^0.235) with P = 29.92126*(1-6.8755856e-6*PA)^5.2558797 gives 7390.37 ft (error −0.63 ft). ICAO ISA (g=9.80665, R=287.05287, L=0.0065 K/m) gives 7373.52 ft (error −17.5 ft). Prefer the NWS formula (or ICAO ISA) over the digitized PA lines for the app; both are well inside the 50 ft target. Digitized 6000 ft PA line at 15 °C is 7366.5 ft.

fig2_55pct_peak_scan_high_da.method: axis_calibration.fig2 maps DA→image row and RPM→column; at each target DA, scan a ±3 px row band for column-wise ink minima, smooth 5 px, keep local minima; 55% curve identified as the RPM peak between the 45% (~2232 RPM) and 65% (~2564 RPM) peaks at the same row (x≈436 px on 733×430 orig).
fig2_55pct_peak_scan_high_da.note: Measured 2398.76 RPM at 11800 DA (rounded 2398.8); curve flat within digitization noise through 12000 ft.

steps: PA (ft) + OAT (°C) → density altitude DA (ft), via the NWS/ICAO formula (preferred) or Fig 1.
DA + RPM → %BHP, from Fig 2 (45/55/65/75% curves) or Fig 4 table (broader %BHP, including 43–85%). Inverse: DA + %BHP → RPM (bisection on the same data, interpolate only).
DA + %BHP → TAS (kt), from Fig 3 (Max Gross Weight, mixture leaned to best power) or Fig 4 table.
DA + RPM → GPH, from Fig 4 table ONLY. The supplement has no separate fuel-flow-vs-%BHP chart.
Full-throttle TAS envelope is the right-hand curve on Fig 3; at a given DA, TAS and %BHP cannot exceed it.
lookup_chain.interpolate_only: Never extrapolate. If PA, OAT, DA, RPM or %BHP falls outside the domain below, the app must show 'Fuera de carta / Out of chart' with the valid range and no numeric result. Sweep cells show '—' with a footnote.

fig1_density_altitude.note: PA lines are MSL (0), 2000, 4000, 6000, 8000, 10000, 12000 ft. High-PA lines leave the top of the chart (e.g. 12000 ft PA exits near OAT ≈ 8–10 °C). MSL enters from the bottom near OAT ≈ −2 °C.

fig2_power.note: 45/55/65% span DA 0–12000. 75% runs from DA ≈ 0 (≈2488 RPM) to DA ≈ 8270 (≈2649 RPM) and stops; 75% is out of chart above that. Below the 45% curve or right of 2800 RPM is out of chart on Fig 2. The table (Fig 4) covers a wider %BHP band at DA 2000–12000.

fig3_speed_power.conditions: Max Gross Weight, Mixture Leaned to Best Power
fig3_speed_power.note: 45/55/65% span DA 0–12000 (65% meets Full Throttle at the top, DA 12000 / ≈127.5 kt). 75% meets Full Throttle at DA 8500 ft / 134.2 kt. TAS is bounded on the right by Full Throttle. Below 45% is out of chart on Fig 3.

fig4_table.temperature: Standard Temperature (table is keyed by Density Altitude, so it is used at any OAT after converting PA+OAT → DA)
fig4_table.note: No sea-level (DA 0) row. No 2600 RPM at 10000 (max is 2550). No 2500 RPM at 12000 (max is 2450). Interpolate only between listed DA and RPM nodes. GPH is only in this table.

nws.description: NOAA/NWS density-altitude formula, matches printed 7391 within 1 ft.

icao_isa.description: ICAO standard-atmosphere inversion (troposphere). Gives 7373.5 ft for the worked example.

fig2_power.title: DA 20-C1 Katana Power Chart  (Figure 2: Power Chart)

75%.note: Printed 75% curve ends between the 8000 and 10000 ft grid lines, near DA 8270 ft / 2650 RPM. Do not extrapolate above this.

fig3_speed_power.title: Speed Power - Cruise Performance, DA 20-C1 Katana  (Figure 3)
fig3_speed_power.conditions: Max Gross Weight, Mixture Leaned to Best Power
fig3_speed_power.flight_test_note: The cruise performance while not a certification requirement, are based on actual flight tests. The actual performance attained will vary from airplane to airplane depending on age and condition of the airframe and powerplants, aircraft rigging and operator technique.

75%.note: 75% meets the Full Throttle envelope at DA 8500 ft, TAS 134.2 kt (gap 0.03 kt). Above this, 75% is not available; use Full Throttle. Do not extrapolate.

Full Throttle.note: Right-hand envelope of the speed-power chart. At a given DA, TAS cannot exceed this curve. 75% meets it at 8500 ft; 65% meets it at the top of the chart (DA 12000 ft, TAS ≈ 127.5 kt).

fig4_cruise_table.title: Figure 4: Cruise Performance
fig4_cruise_table.subtitle: Table to calculate maximum endurance and range depending on the available fuel.
gph_notes: Fuel flow (GPH) is given only in this table, versus density altitude and RPM, at standard temperature. There is no fuel-flow-vs-%BHP chart in the supplement.
GPH generally declines with %BHP, but is not a clean function of %BHP alone (scatter of several tenths of a gallon).

The 10000 ft / 2200 RPM GPH of 3.3 and the 12000 ft / 2200 RPM GPH of 1.7 are clearly the printed figures (confirmed at 6× on the original JPEG) but are physically suspicious: neighbouring 2300 RPM values are 5.1 and 4.6, and the drop from 4.4 at 8000/2200 is very steep. Transcribed as printed; treat as uncertain if used for endurance.
4000 ft / 2700 RPM GPH is 8.8, slightly higher than 2000 ft / 2700 RPM at 8.7 despite lower %BHP (83 vs 85). As printed.
